KEY MESSAGE 1...

A warm front is currently slowly lifting north and east across the 
forecast area this afternoon. By 5 PM the front should make it to 
the I-90 corridor between Syracuse and Utica. South of this boundary 
skies will become partly sunny, temperatures will rise into the 
upper 70s and lower 80s along with dew points near 70F. This will 
allow mixed layer CAPE to increase upwards of 500-1000J/kg during 
the early evening hours. A few isolated storms could develop out 
ahead of the next incoming wave now located over lower Michigan. 
Otherwise, as this wave moves in a line of showers and thunderstorms 
will press east arriving in the Finger Lakes and Central Southern 
Tier by around 8-9 PM. The line of showers and storms reaches Utica--
Ithaca and Elmira by late evening, then Binghamton, Scranton and 
Monticello after midnight and into the very early predawn hours 
Thursday. As this line of showers and storms slowly presses south 
and east across the area a few storms could produce gusty to 
isolated damaging winds and there is even an isolated tornado risk 
(mainly in or near Steuben County). Since the storms will be 
relatively slow moving, some training of heavy rainfall is also 
possible, but the flash flood risk is marginal. The showers and 
storms are forecast to exit NE PA and the southern Catskills between 
3-6 AM early Thursday morning. Overnight lows will be mild in the 
mid to upper 60s with some patchy fog possible.

KEY MESSAGE 2...

The showers and frontal boundary will be well south of the area on 
Thursday as winds shift to west-northwest and become a little breezy 
during the day (7-15 mph, gusts to 25 mph. Skies should be mostly 
sunny through the day and highs look to reach the mid-70s to lower 
80s. Dew points gradually fall through the day as drier air advects 
in on the northwest flow. It will be much cooler and more refreshing 
Thursday nigh as surface high pressure moves into the region. Expect 
decreasing clouds from NW to SE through the night, some patchy fog 
late and lows mainly in the 50s. 

Friday will see a strong 1018mb surface high directly overhead 
through the day. This will mean sunny skies, lighter winds and high 
temperatures in the low to mid-70s. Went slightly above the NBM 
guidance for highs, closer to the bias corrected guidance 
considering the increasing heights and temperatures aloft through 
the day. 

Friday night will likely be the coolest night of the week. High 
pressure slowly slides east and a stronger low level inversion is 
likely to form as warmer air aloft arrives. Widespread valley fog is 
likely to develop in these ideal radiational cooling conditions; 
lows drop into the mid-40s to lower 50s areawide.

Saturday will feature gradually increasing clouds from southwest to 
northeast as the surface high retreats off the New England coast. 
Instability looks to remain mainly west of our forecast area through 
Saturday afternoon and evening as we maintain a southerly/southeast 
maritime influenced air mass. As winds turn south and 1000-500mb 
thicknesses rise above 570dm, expect warm temperatures in the mid-
70s to lower 80s and gradually increasing humidity later in the day. 
Most of the shower activity is forecast to hold off until after 
sunset, expect there is a slight chance to low end chance for a few 
late day showers over western areas of the CWA.

KEY MESSAGE 3...

A flat upper level shortwave and weak surface front are forecast to 
push through the region Saturday night into Sunday. This will bring 
a round of scattered to numerous showers, with a chance for 
thunderstorms as well (mainly Sunday afternoon). This system looks 
weakly force and instability marginal. Temperatures remain warm in 
the mid-70s to low 80s on Sunday as there should be some 
intermittent breaks in the clouds. It is not looking like a washout, 
but instead just occasional showers or thunderstorms. Shear and 
instability are looking low on the latest guidance, so at this time 
we are not expecting organize strong or severe convection.

There is more uncertainty in the model guidance and forecast heading 
into early next week. Current indications are then Monday will be 
dry and seasonably as upper level heights gradually amplify over the 
area. Tuesday will be mainly dry and warmer as a southerly flow 
takes hold and 1000-500mb thicknesses potentially surge past 576dm A 
front then attempts to approach by the middle of next week, but 
could also washout as it heads into the mid and upper level ridge 
along the East Coast. 500mb heights remain above average over the 
region Monday through Wednesday, generally around 590dm.
